newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jababeka says land ruling beneficial.
newsitem.headline: Jababeka says land ruling beneficial.

text.p: Indonesian property firm PT Kawasan Industri Jababeka (KIJ) said on Tuesday it should benefit from a recent government decision to halt approvals for new industrial estates in the West Java region.

Jababeka, an industrial estate developer, says it holds enough land to meet customer demand in the heavily populated region adjacent to the capital of Jakarta, and the heartland of Indonesia's manufacturing sector.
"The regulation is likely to have a positive impact on us as the competition is not likely to get fiercer," KIJ finance director Paulus Supartio told Reuters.
"As for Jababeka, we don't have to acquire new sites for several years. We have a land bank which is enough until the year 2000 or even a few years after that," Supartio said.
Supartio said Jababeka has a land bank of around 2,880 hectares (7129 acres) in its industrial estates, including in the West Java regions of Cikarang and Cilegon.
Land Minister Soni Harsono said in late September that the government had suspended approvals for new industrial estates in West Java until the year 2000.
Harsono said his ministry had already given permits for industrial estates covering at least 25,000 hectares (62,000 acres) in West Java, enough to meet demand until 2000.
West Java traditionally attracts large investment funds and has the country's largest concentration of industrial estates.

"PT KIJ has obtained land permits for industrial investment covering 800 hectares (2,000 acres ) in Cilegon, West Java, and (the permit) was being processed to be increased to 1,300 hectares (3,210 acres)," Supartio said.
"Investors are likely to reap the benefits of its convenient location as it is only between five to ten kilometres from the huge Bojonegara seaport," Supartio said.
He said the firm expected to expand the industrial site to 1,800 hectares (4450 acres) from 1,300 hectares (3210 acres) following land reclamation for the development of a jetty.
PT Bina Jasa Hantarindo, controlled by President Suharto's son Bambang Trihatmodjo, has started construction of a huge deep-water port in Bojonegara that was expected to start operating in 1998.

The port is expected to replace Tanjung Priok in Jakarta as the country's main seaport, and handle the latest generation of container ships that draw up to 18 metres (60 feet) and have a capacity of more than 6,000 twenty-feet equivalent units (TEUs).
Supartio said the company expected to spend around 400 billion rupiah (US$172 million) to acquire the Cilegon land site. Development of the site was expected to start in 1997.
Jababeka corporate secretary Budianto Liman said the Cilegon industrial estate was expected to attract both local and foreign investors and to boost sales in the coming years.
"In terms of land size, around 65 percent of the land was sold last year to foreign firms while the rest to locals. The composition is likely to remain the same this year," Liman said.
Foreign firms located in the company's estates include Britain's ICI, Japan's Kao Corp, RJR Nabisco and Unilever, he said.
